cohort: 474 singleton pregnancies between 18-24 weeks of gestation were enrolled and followed until delivery.
finding: Lateral placentation at mid-trimester was significantly associated with increased risk of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, preterm labour, IUGR, and lower mean birth weight.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates were significantly higher in the lateral placental group (52.2%) compared to anterior and posterior groups (~30%).
